newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA ISSUE DEPT ASSETS RISE TO 3.2 BLN MARKS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA ISSUE DEPT ASSETS RISE TO 3.2 BLN MARKS.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) Issue Department assets and liabilities rose to 3.196 billion marks on July 18 from 3.08 billion marks a week earlier, the BNB said on Monday.

The cash in nostro and vostro accounts in foreign currencies of the assets fell to the equivalent of 1.391 trillion levs on July 18 from 1.444 trillion levs a week earlier while the BNB holdings in foreign securities rose to the equivalent of 1.16 trillion levs from 990 billion, the BNB said in a statement.
BNB officials were not immidately available for comment.

The department's assets included the mark equivalent of 1.16 billion levs in foreign securities, 1.391 trillion levs cash and nostro accounts in foreign currencies, 640.7 billion levs in monetary gold and 5.2 billion levs in accrued interest receivable, the BNB said in a statement.
Currency in circulation, a part of Issue Department liabilities rose to 774.1 billion levs on July 18 from 714.5 billion levs a week earlier.

The department's liabilities also comprised 705.8 billion levs in bank deposits and current accounts, 608.3 billion levs in government deposits and accounts and 584.8 billion levs in the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development account.
Part of the liabilities also were 6.1 billion levs in other deposits and accrued interest payable of 0.8 billion levs.
The liabilities also included a 516.2 billion lev deposit of the BNB Banking Department that can be lent to sound banks only in case of systemic risk for the banking and payments system.
The primary objective of the Banking Department is to ensure confidence in the liquidity of the banking system and more broadly the efficient functioning of key financial markets.

Under an agreement with the International Monetary Fund Bulgaria introduced on July 1 the currency board system, a fixed exchange rate mechanism which requires levs in circulation to be matched by BNB foreign exchange reserves.
Under the arrangement the lev is pegged to the mark as anchor currency at 1,000 levs. The system bans central bank lending to the government and commercial banks. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
